newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey expects 15 pct rise in 1997 textile exports.
newsitem.headline: Turkey expects 15 pct rise in 1997 textile exports.

text.p: Turkish exporters expect a 15-percent rise in total textile sales this year after a drop in exports of about two percent in 1996, Turkey Exporters' Council (TIM) officials said.

Okan Oguz, president of the council, told reporters they expected the European Union market, the top customer of Turkish textile products, to grow by 2.5 percent this year after some shrinkage in 1996.
"Political certainty and a stronger dollar in recent months are positive factors for exports," he said.
"Investments started last year will increase the production capacity of the textile industry this year. Therefore we expect a 15 percent rise in textile exports," he said.

Turkey's total textile exports, mainly ready-to-wear items and other textile raw material, totalled $8.79 billion in 1996, down from $9 billion a year ago, according to the unofficial but reliable TIM data. Turkey's total exports were $23.69 billion in 1996, up from $22.4 billion in 1995, TIM said.
Textile producers blamed an overvalued Turkish lira in 1996 and higher prices of raw material and other production inputs for the decline in textile exports, Turkey's top money spinner.
Another factor which also slowed textile sales was Turkey's customs union deal with the European Union which took effect in January 1996.
According to the deal, Turkey applied new tariffs for its trade with third countries, and that caused losses in textile customers and reduced exports.
Oguz said the influential council would take steps to boost lobbying in the United States to have U.S. quotas on Turkish textile products abolsihed.
"We will also target Japan as a new market. It is difficult to enter but easy to stay in," he said.
